content: Cefaclor is administered orally. For adults, the standard dosage is 250 mg every 8 hours. In cases of more severe infections, such as pneumonia, or infections caused by less susceptible organisms, the dosage may be increased to double the usual amount. For pediatric patients, the typical recommended daily dosage is 20 mg per kilogram of body weight, divided into doses given every 8 hours. In more serious infections, such as otitis media or infections caused by less susceptible organisms, a dosage of 40 mg per kilogram per day is recommended, with a maximum daily dosage not exceeding 1 gram. Cefaclor can be administered to patients with impaired renal function. In such cases, the dosage generally remains unchanged (refer to the Precautions section for further details). When treating β-hemolytic streptococcal infections, cefaclor should be administered at a therapeutic dosage for a minimum duration of 10 days.
